recognize_zh: 低倍抹片中充滿中等大小的母細胞樣細胞，細胞核圓至略不規則、染色質細緻，灰藍色細胞質常偏向一側形成「手鏡／尾巴」狀，部分周邊有小空泡，這種無顆粒的母細胞搭配皮膚病灶應考慮 BPDCN。
features: Markedly increased medium-sized blastoid cells dominating the nucleated cell population
Round to slightly irregular nuclei with fine chromatin and high N:C ratio
Scant to moderate agranular grey-blue cytoplasm, often polarized to one side (hand-mirror/tail-like)
Occasional small cytoplasmic vacuoles near the cell membrane
Few residual small lymphocytes and occasional nucleated red cells; no Auer rods or granules seen
describe_en: Low-power view of a Wright-stained smear (likely peripheral blood, given the red cell monolayer and paucity of maturing granulocytes) shows a marked increase in medium-sized blastoid cells. The cells have round to mildly irregular nuclei with fine chromatin, a high N:C ratio and scant to moderate agranular grey-blue cytoplasm that is frequently polarized, forming tail-like or hand-mirror extensions, with occasional small peripheral vacuoles. No Auer rods or cytoplasmic granules are seen. The morphology is that of an agranular blastic neoplasm and is not lineage-specific; with the CD4+/CD56+/CD123+ phenotype, findings are consistent with blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.

ddx.dx: Acute myeloid leukemia with monocytic differentiation
ddx.vs: Monoblasts/promonocytes usually have more abundant cytoplasm, fine granules and folded nuclei with nonspecific esterase or MPO activity, whereas BPDCN blasts are agranular and cytochemically negative.
Lymphoblasts look similar but express cytoplasmic CD3 and TdT, which are negative in this case.
Sezary cells have cerebriform convoluted nuclei with condensed chromatin rather than the fine blastic chromatin seen here.
